chunks: "Ibn Mas'ud corrupted the people's salat (prayer) with two things: by his saying, 'Blessed is Your Name and Exalted is Your Majesty,' and this is something the jinn said out of ignorance, and Allah, the Exalted, related it from them; and by his saying, 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.'

key_terms.أَفْسَدَ: corrupted or invalidly altered in the context of ritual practice
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ الل: Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah, the second phrase criticized here
key_terms.الْجِنُّ: the jinn, whose speech is referenced in the hadith
key_terms.بِجَهَالَةٍ: out of ignorance, describing how that statement was uttered
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ: Blessed is Your Name, a liturgical phrase mentioned in the report
key_terms.تَعَالَى جَدُّكَ: Exalted is Your Majesty, a phrase criticized here in prayer usage
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُمْ: their salat (prayer), meaning the ritual prayer of the people

ai.seo_question: Which phrases did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say Ibn Mas'ud introduced into salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام criticizes the inclusion of certain phrases in salat (prayer) and presents them as corrupting the proper form of the prayer. It also identifies one phrase as originating from the speech of the jinn and being cited by Allah, the Exalted, rather than prescribed as part of ritual worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1191 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Ibn Mas'ud corrupted people's prayers with two things: by saying 'Blessed be Your Name, and Exalted is Your Majesty,' which was something the jinn said ignorantly, and Allah (swt), the Exalted, narrated it from them, and by saying 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt)'."
